title: half-life-v1
learningObjectives: Explain how half-life describes the time for half of a radioactive sample to decay
Calculate remaining amount from initial amount, half-life, and elapsed time using exponential decay
Compare decay rates for isotopes with short and long half-lives

explanations.text: Radioactive materials lose activity over time as unstable isotopes break down into harmless products.

evidence.quote: Radioactive isotopes eventually decay, or disintegrate, to harmless materials.

explanations.text: The time required for half of a radioactive sample to decay defines its half-life, which varies widely among isotopes.

evidence.quote: Strontium-90 and cesium-137 have half-lives of about 30 years (half the radioactivity will decay in 30 years).
Plutonium-239 has a half-life of 24,000 years.

explanations.text: Different radioactive wastes are produced during energy generation, medical applications, and research operations.

evidence.quote: Radioactive (or nuclear) waste is a byproduct from nuclear reactors, fuel processing plants, hospitals and research facilities.

predictions.prompt: A 100 gram sample with a 5 year half-life after 5 years
A 240 gram sample with a 6 year half-life after 12 years
A 500 gram sample with an 8 year half-life after 20 years
